from .models import Subscription


def current_period(sub: Subscription, at: datetime) -> tuple[datetime, datetime]:
    """Return the [start, end) billing period of ``sub`` that contains ``at``."""
    at = ensure_utc(at)
    start = ensure_utc(sub.started_at)
    if at < start:
        raise BillingError("before_start", at.isoformat())
    length = timedelta(days=sub.period_days)
    n = (at - start) // length
    period_start = start + n * length
    return period_start, period_start + length

def current_period(sub: Subscription, at: datetime) -> tuple[datetime, datetime]:
    """Return the [start, end) billing period of ``sub`` that contains ``at``."""
    at = ensure_utc(at)
    start = ensure_utc(sub.started_at)
    if at < start:
        raise BillingError("before_start", at.isoformat())
    length = timedelta(days=sub.period_days)
    n = (at - start) // length

from datetime import date, datetime, time, timedelta

from .clock import ensure_utc


def day_bounds(day: date) -> tuple[datetime, datetime]:
    start = datetime.combine(day, time.min)

def total_amount(payments) -> float:

def payments_between(payments, start, end):
    """Payments created in [start, end), oldest first.

    Boundaries are normalized to UTC so aware datetimes from different
    timezones compare correctly. Payments without a ``created_at`` are
    excluded, and the window is half-open: ``start`` is included while
    ``end`` is not.
    """
    start = ensure_utc(start)
    end = ensure_utc(end)
    selected = [
        payment
        for payment in payments
        if payment.created_at is not None
        and start <= ensure_utc(payment.created_at) < end
    ]
    return sorted(selected, key=lambda payment: ensure_utc(payment.created_at))
EOF
